rect.data-title: 12A Security: current coverage and proposed baseline

g.textArea: 12A Security: current coverage and proposed baseline
CTO / IT / DevOps / product owners | Security extends beyond laptops; verify protection separately for each environment.
Draft for team review | Blue: proposed | Neutral: documented context | Yellow: gap or decision
Documented current state
Proposed baseline

rect.data-content:
Employee and contractor devices
Falcon is required; enrollment and effective policies must be checked.
Complete fleet compliance has not been verified.

Google Cloud posture and foundations
Falcon posture monitoring is reported active across 64 projects.
The Nov 2 audit records private GKE/SQL, workload identity and backups.

LMS runtime and Cloud Workstations
Staging/production GKE sensing remains an open rollout task.
Cloud Workstations has sensor health gaps and a canary in progress.

Scanning, access and logging
Registry read-access source exists; live scanning needs verification.
Recheck dated privileged-access, key and audit-log findings.

Identity and access
Agreed Entra identities and minimum normal access.
Controlled temporary elevation and verified removal.

Runtime and image coverage
Supported sensors and working registry/image scans.
Check exact targets, policies and useful security signals.

Cloud, network and data
Reviewed posture findings and restricted access.
Secret references, appropriate test data and recovery checks.

Logs and response
Required events, delivery checks and agreed retention.
Named alert responders, escalation and a tested runbook.

g.textArea: Roles to confirm with the team and partners

rect.data-content:
TrekAI IT / DevOps
Own device/platform implementation.
Agree accountable security and incident owners.

MOXFIVE
Documented incident response and controls review.
Confirm current engagement and escalation duties.

At-Bay
Documented post-incident hardening and M365/SSO work.
Confirm current scope and handoffs.

Team decision
Agree the required baseline, accountable owner, partner duties and first rollout scope. Record unsupported targets and approved exceptions.

g.textArea: 12B Security: rollout, verification and response
IT / DevOps / security responders / partners | Proposed workflow | A control is complete when the target is protected and its signals reach an owner.
Draft for team review | Blue: proposed | Neutral: documented context | Yellow: gap or decision
Implementation and acceptance

rect.data-content:
1. Inventory targets
List systems and controls.
Confirm live coverage.
Assign each gap.

2. Review the change
Confirm supported model.
Review code, permissions
and rollback.

3. Prove in staging
Deploy a small pilot.
Check workload health
and security telemetry.

4. Expand by target
Approve production.
Roll out in stages.
Record acceptance.

Validation fails
Hold rollout. Fix or roll back.
Keep the gap assigned.

g.textArea: Acceptance checks for each target

rect.data-content:
Runtime protection
Fresh check-in and intended policy.
Safe test yields exact-target events.

Image scanning
Working registry connection and scan.
Match the deployed image digest.

Logs and alerts
Required events arrive and parse.
A test alert reaches the responder.

g.textArea: Alert and incident workflow

rect.data-content:
Detect and route
Identify product and environment.

Assess and assign
Record impact and incident owner.

Contain and recover
Authorized response and partner help.

Review and improve
Verify recovery and assign follow-ups.

g.textArea: Agree coverage hours, response targets, backup contacts and containment authority. Preserve investigation records and use the existing incident process.

Delivery work packages

rect.data-content:
1. Confirm coverage
Inventory controls by target.
Check live health and open findings.
Prioritize gaps and propose owners.

2. Agree the baseline
Agree required controls and checks.
Confirm vendor scope and responders.
Set exception and approval rules.

3. Prove the changes
Pilot supported sensing, scans and logs.
Check health and safe test signals.
Exercise response in staging.

4. Expand and maintain
Approve each production rollout.
Add checks to templates and releases.
Recheck after lifecycle changes.

g.textArea: Coverage record: separate controls and targets

rect.data-content:
Products and environments
Hub/LMS: development, QA, staging and production.
CAP/TrekFinder: RD and each agreed additional target.
Track devices and Cloud Workstations separately.

Record for every applicable control
Exact target, required coverage, actual status and latest check.
Owner, gap or approved exception, and next review.
Statuses: verified / configured but unverified / gap / exception.

g.textArea: QA template and handoff

rect.data-content:
Include security in the approved template
Scoped identity, network isolation and secret references.
Applicable runtime protection, scanning and security logs.
Agreed test-data, retention, expiry and cleanup rules.

Verify before QA receives the URL
DevOps owns template and readiness checks; QA requests approved options.
A failed required control holds handoff unless an exception is approved.
Cleanup ends temporary access and preserves required records.

g.textArea: Initial priorities and dependencies

rect.data-content:
Prioritize from verified impact
LMS staging/production sensing, Cloud Workstations canary, registry scanning and the highest-impact access/logging findings.
Coordinate with Terraform/GitOps delivery, Entra/PAM, QA requests, observability and documentation.

g.textArea: Decisions for the team

rect.data-content:
Who owns security and response? Which controls block release or QA handoff?
What do MOXFIVE and At-Bay currently cover? Who approves exceptions and production rollout?
